question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -12 \\ -15\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -12 \\ -15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -12 \\ -15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -12 \\ -15\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=8 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-12 \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$, the second equation by $2$, and adding the resulting equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}23{x}_{2} &=0 \\ {x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=0$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-12 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4(0) &=-12 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=-12 \\ {x}_{1} &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-4$ and ${x}_{2}=0$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ 4(-4)-3(0) &=-15 \\ -16 &=-15\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 0 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 0 \\ -9\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 0 \\ -9\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 0 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=12 \\ -{x}_{2} &=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=0$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=0$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=12 \\ 3{x}_{1}-8(0) &=12 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=12 \\ {x}_{1} &=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=0$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ -2(4)+4(0) &=-9 \\ -8 &=-9\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-31 \\ 17 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-31 \\ 17 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-7{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-31 \\ 17 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-31 \\ 17 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} &=-31 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=17 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ {x}_{2} &=7\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=7$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=17 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5(7) &=17 \\ -3{x}_{1} &=-18 \\ {x}_{1} &=6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=7$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ (6)-(7) &=-1 \\ -1 &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=7$, which means

$$
6{a}_{1}+7{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(6)+(7)=13.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-10 \\ 8 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-10 \\ 8 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-10 \\ 8 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-10 \\ 8 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-10 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=8 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the second equation by $2$ and adding the result to the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} &=6 \\ {x}_{2} &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-2$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=8 \\ {x}_{1}-2(-2) &=8 \\ {x}_{1} &=4 \\ {x}_{1} &=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=-2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-3 \\ -2(4)-3(-2) &=-3 \\ -2 &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ - \frac{39}{2}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ - \frac{39}{2}\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1} \\ 7{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ - \frac{39}{2}\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ - \frac{39}{2}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{39}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $-2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1} &=3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 5(3)+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ {x}_{2} &=- \frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=- \frac{11}{2}$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{39}{2} \\ -(3)+3\left(- \frac{11}{2}\right) &=- \frac{39}{2} \\ - \frac{39}{2} &=- \frac{39}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=- \frac{11}{2}$, which means

$$
3{a}_{1}- \frac{11}{2}{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(3)+\left(- \frac{11}{2}\right)=- \frac{5}{2}.
$$
